assumptions: A retried order is one with more than one payment attempt.
caveats: Part of this answer uses custom SQL written by the AI, outside the governed semantic layer. It was validated (read-only, governed views only, role filters applied) before running, but its logic has not been reviewed like the governed metrics.

Duplicate records on 12 Oct: 341 attempts were ingested twice (11,704 raw rows vs 11,363 unique attempts, +3.0%). Paysight counts each attempt once; duplicates were removed in the clean view, keeping the first ingestion.

Volume spike 18 Oct-31 Oct: attempt volume was +39% versus the usual level for those weekdays over 14 days. Real business events (sales) and data gaps both look like this, so check before comparing totals across this period. It is not a data error by itself and is flagged for context.

facts.text: 10,865 of 419,385 orders in October 2026 had more than one payment attempt, a retried fraction of 2.6%.
The remaining orders were paid or failed on a single attempt, with no retry.
Attempt volume ran about 39% above the usual weekday level from 18 Oct to 31 Oct, a period that falls inside the October window.

response.headline: About 2.6% of October 2026 orders (10,865 of 419,385) needed at least one retry, meaning more than one payment attempt.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Compute the retried fraction separately for 1-17 Oct and 18-31 Oct and compare.
hypotheses.rationale: Higher volume and different traffic mix can shift retry behaviour, but the evidence only shows the spike, not its effect on retries.
hypotheses.text: The 18-31 Oct volume spike (likely a sale) may have changed the retry share relative to a normal month.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: The 18-31 Oct volume spike may have changed the retry share relative to a normal month.
recommendations.rationale: A single monthly number hides whether retries are driven by the late-October surge or by specific methods.
recommendations.text: Split the retry fraction by period (before and during the volume spike) and by payment method to see where retries concentrate.
